---
title: "Summary of July and August Stream Temperature Trends"
format: html
editor: visual
---

## Overview

This analysis examined long-term stream temperature trends at multiple Willamette River monitoring sites during July and August from 2010–2023.

## Key Findings

The July analysis showed stronger warming trends than August across monitoring locations. July stream temperatures demonstrated statistically significant relationships with year and site, suggesting that warming patterns differed among locations.

The August analysis also showed increasing temperatures over time, although statistical relationships were weaker than those observed in July.

## Management Implications

Increasing summer stream temperatures may contribute to thermal stress for aquatic organisms and reduce the availability of suitable cold-water habitat. Continued warming trends could have implications for fisheries management and watershed conservation planning.

## Example Visualization

```{r}

library(tidyverse)

temp_data <- read_csv("willamette_temp.csv")

july_data <- subset(temp_data, month == "Jul")

ggplot(july_data,
       aes(x = year,
           y = temp_C,
           color = factor(site_no))) +

  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +

  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +

  labs(
    title = "July Stream Temperature Trends",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Temperature (°C)",
    color = "Site Number"
  ) +

  theme_minimal()

```
